insights.title: Card charge-off guidance lowered to 3.2%
insights.summary: Full-year 2026 card net charge-off rate guidance was about 3.4% on the Q4 2025 call and continued at about 3.4% on the Q1 2026 call. On the Q2 2026 call it was lowered to about 3.2%, which management attributed to better-than-expected consumer credit performance.
insights.uw_relevance: A lower guided card loss rate points to stronger consumer credit in a large consumer book. This is management's own guidance and attribution, not an independent view of loss trends.

insights.title: Expense guidance raised on volume-driven costs
insights.summary: Adjusted 2026 expense guidance was about $105 billion on the Q4 2025 call and was unchanged on the Q1 2026 call. The Q2 2026 call raised it to about $107.5 billion, primarily on volume and revenue-related expenses. The CEO also said growth might slow in 2027 or 2028.
insights.uw_relevance: A higher expense base and an ongoing investment cycle affect the operating cost and earnings trajectory. The company links the increase mainly to costs that move with revenue, which management describes as the reason for the change.

insights.title: Capital rule criticism sharpens across calls
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call the CFO declined to give a full critique of the G-SIB framework. On the Q1 2026 call management said the G-SIB proposal was bad for international competitiveness and set out specific objections. On the Q2 2026 call the CEO criticised the regulators' method directly and said the numbers were being falsely done.
insights.uw_relevance: Public opposition to proposed capital rules signals how the company is positioning in an active rulemaking that sets its capital requirements. It does not indicate the rule outcome.

insights.title: Private credit underwriting weakness acknowledged
insights.summary: The Q4 2025 call said the company was quite mindful of the risks in nonbank financial institution lending. The Q1 2026 call said there had been some weakening in underwriting beyond private credit. The Q2 2026 call described some players with weaker covenants, more PIK and more rollover risk.
insights.uw_relevance: Weaker underwriting in leveraged and private credit bears on the risk profile of exposures the company describes as structurally protected. The shift is in management's own assessment of the market.

insights.title: Macro optimism tempered by peak-cycle caveats
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call the CEO called the short-run macro outlook pretty positive while calling geopolitical risk an enormous amount of risk. On the Q1 2026 call the company flagged Middle East developments as a possible drag on deal execution. On the Q2 2026 call the CEO said conditions were close to as good as it gets and that their duration was unknown.
insights.uw_relevance: Management describing current conditions as near peak with uncertain duration matters for how market-linked revenue and current earnings are read. It is not a forecast of a downturn.

insights.title: Buybacks framed behind client deployment
insights.summary: On the Q4 2025 call buybacks were described as the alternative when deployment returns fall below 17%. On the Q1 2026 call the CEO said the preferred use of capital was building businesses and serving clients, not buybacks for their own sake. On the Q2 2026 call he said the firm could do far more than the figure it mentioned or nothing at all. Share repurchases were $8.32B in FY2026 Q1 and $6.79B in FY2026 Q2.
insights.uw_relevance: A shift in emphasis between capital return and client investment bears on how much capital is returned to shareholders. These are reported statements of priority, not a view on the buyback programme.

followups.question: What drove the CET1 ratio decline from 15.7% in FY2024 to 14.2% in FY2026 Q2, and what does the preliminary FY2026 Q3 figure of 13.9% reflect?
followups.summary: The CET1 ratio was 15.7% in FY2024 and 14.2% in FY2026 Q2, and the preliminary FY2026 Q3 figure is 13.9%. The Tier 1 capital ratio was 15.1% at FY2026 Q2, down from 16.8% in FY2024.
followups.uw_relevance: A falling capital ratio reduces the cushion available to absorb losses, which bears directly on balance sheet review under D&O.

followups.question: How does the company reconcile the cited $40 billion of excess capital and the planned dividend increase to $1.65 with a CET1 ratio that has declined to 14.2%?
followups.summary: Share repurchases were $31.59B in FY2025 against $18.83B in FY2024. Management cites about $40 billion of excess capital, and the board intends to raise the quarterly dividend to $1.65 from the third quarter.
followups.uw_relevance: Large distributions reduce the capital available to absorb losses, so the capital plan bears on balance sheet context for D&O.

followups.question: How has the estimated uninsured deposit base of $1,743.90B at FY2026 Q2 behaved since the 64.3% share was reached, and which client segments hold the largest balances?
followups.summary: Estimated uninsured deposits were $1,743.90B at FY2026 Q2, against $1,558.60B at FY2025 Q4. Uninsured deposits rose to 64.3% of total deposits from 60.9%.
followups.uw_relevance: A rising uninsured deposit base raises liquidity stress exposure, which D&O reviewers weigh when assessing oversight of funding risk.

followups.question: What drove the liquidity coverage ratio down to 110.0% at FY2026 Q2 from 113.0% a year earlier, and how much of the high-quality liquid asset buffer is available for further outflows?
followups.summary: The liquidity coverage ratio was 110.0% at FY2026 Q2 against 113.0% at FY2025 Q2. Unrealized losses on AFS and HTM securities were $18.24B at FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: A narrowing liquidity buffer alongside rising uninsured deposits is a liquidity stress indicator relevant to D&O review of the balance sheet.

followups.question: How much of the $18.24B of unrealized losses on AFS and HTM securities would affect capital or liquidity if these positions were sold, and what hedging is in place?
followups.summary: Unrealized losses on AFS and HTM securities were $18.24B at FY2026 Q2, up from $17.05B at FY2025 Q4. These losses equal 4.9% of stockholders' equity at FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: Large unrealized losses relative to equity can constrain capital and liquidity in a stress scenario, which bears on D&O balance sheet review.

followups.question: What is the basis of the Florida suit filed in January 2026 naming the bank and its CEO, and has the company made any accrual or disclosure for it?
followups.summary: A civil lawsuit filed in January 2026 in Florida state court by President Donald J. Trump and affiliated entities names JPMorgan Chase Bank N.A. and its CEO. The outcome is not yet known.
followups.uw_relevance: An open suit naming the bank and its CEO is a direct D&O litigation exposure with an outcome not yet known.

followups.question: How are the $50B of private credit exposures tied to leveraged loan investors split by borrower quality, covenant protection and PIK usage, given the weaker underwriting the company now describes?
followups.summary: Management cites about $160B of core NBFI exposure, of which about $50B is private credit tied to leveraged loan investors. The Q2 2026 call described some players with weaker covenants, more PIK and more rollover risk.
followups.uw_relevance: Concentrated non-bank lending exposure with a flagged loss risk is a company-specific credit risk that D&O reviewers assess.

followups.question: What data supports lowering the full-year 2026 card net charge-off guidance to about 3.2% when the allowance for loan losses to loans ratio has stayed at 1.8%?
followups.summary: Full-year 2026 card net charge-off guidance was about 3.4% on the Q1 2026 call and was lowered to about 3.2% on the Q2 2026 call, which management attributed to better-than-expected consumer credit performance. The allowance ratio was 1.8% at FY2026 Q2.
followups.uw_relevance: A guidance change based on management's own attribution needs independent support when assessing credit quality for D&O purposes.

followups.question: What succession plan is in place for the President and COO role after Daniel Pinto retires at the end of 2026, and who will hold accountability for CIB, CCB and operational risk during the transition?
followups.summary: Two CIB Co-CEOs were elected Co-Presidents effective immediately. President and COO Daniel Pinto will retire at the end of 2026, and Marianne Lake, former CCB CEO, is retiring.
followups.uw_relevance: Turnover across the top management team bears on key-person and succession exposure under D&O review.

followups.question: What oversight responsibilities does the lead independent director hold under the combined Chair and CEO structure, and has the board filled the seat vacated by Todd A. Combs?
followups.summary: Todd A. Combs notified the company of his resignation from the Board effective December 7, 2025, and the filing states it was not the result of any disagreement. The 2026 proxy confirms the CEO also serves as chair, with a lead independent director in place.
followups.uw_relevance: Board turnover and a combined Chair and CEO structure are governance points that D&O underwriting review considers directly.

followups.question: What trading plans or other basis support officer sales of 6.8% of holdings in FY2026 Q2, and how do these sales relate to the company's own disclosures?
followups.summary: Holdings sold by officers were 6.8% in FY2026 Q2, up from 2.9% in FY2026 Q1 and 1.6% in FY2025 Q4. Insider net open-market sales were $69M in FY2026 Q2, against $55M in FY2026 Q1.

followups.uw_relevance: A large portfolio acquisition with a long integration period adds operational and integration risk to the company profile.

followups.question: What is FY2026 Q2 net income excluding the $4.6 billion Visa gain and the $1.0 billion of equity investment gains, and how will these non-recurring items be presented in future periods?
followups.summary: Visa's acceptance of the Firm's Class B-2 share tender on May 11, 2026 produced a $4.6 billion net gain. Q2 2026 also included $1.0 billion of gains on certain equity investments, and reported net income was $21.16B.
followups.uw_relevance: Non-recurring gains lift the reported quarter, so underwriters need to separate them from underlying earnings when reviewing financial reporting quality.

metric_relevance.buyback_intensity: Buybacks equaled 0.32x net income in FY2026 Q2, down from 0.50x in Q1 and 0.63x in FY2025 Q4. The ratio also reflects net income lifted by the Visa gain, so the drop overstates the change in buyback pace.
metric_relevance.buybacks: Share repurchases fell to $6.79B in FY2026 Q2 from $8.32B in Q1, after $31.59B in FY2025. Management is keeping capital for organic deployment while capital ratios are declining, which draws scrutiny on the buyback pause.
metric_relevance.cet1_ratio: Standardized CET1 fell from 15.7% at FY2024 Q4 to a preliminary 13.9% in FY2026 Q3, with RWA up about $52 billion in the quarter alone. Management's planned 5.2% G-SIB requirement for 2028, up 70 basis points from 4.5%, makes this the central capital question.
metric_relevance.deposit_growth_yoy: Deposit growth was 5.9% YoY in FY2026 Q2 after 7.2% in Q1 and 6.4% at FY2025 year-end, following 0.2% at FY2024 Q4. Recent deposit gains are concentrated in a base where the uninsured share is rising.
metric_relevance.deposits: Total deposits reached $2,713.70B in FY2026 Q2, up from $2,559.32B at FY2025 year-end. Uninsured deposits make up 64.3% of this total, so the funding base depends on depositor confidence.
metric_relevance.equity: Stockholders' equity rose to $374.60B in FY2026 Q2 from $362.44B at FY2025 year-end, yet the standardized CET1 ratio still fell over the same period as RWA rose about $52 billion in the quarter.
metric_relevance.fee_income_growth_yoy: Fee income growth was 46.7% YoY in FY2026 Q2 against 11.0% in Q1, and it was driven mainly by the Visa gain. Investment banking fees grew 14% YoY in the Q3 call versus 30% in Q2, showing activity cooling from its peak.
metric_relevance.lcr: The liquidity coverage ratio was 110% in FY2026 Q2, down from 113% in FY2025 Q2. The decline comes as uninsured deposits rose to 64.3% of total deposits, which makes the liquidity buffer a central question.
metric_relevance.loan_loss_reserve_ratio: The allowance for loan losses was 1.8% of loans in FY2026 Q2, down from 1.9% through FY2025 Q3 and steady since FY2025 Q4. Reserve adequacy will be tested by the private credit terms management describes as loosening and by card guidance.
metric_relevance.net_income: Net income reached $21.16B in FY2026 Q2 with the Visa gain and then $15.30B in FY2026 Q3, against $57.05B for FY2025. Earnings in the 2026 quarters depend on a one-time item, so the post-gain quarter is the more relevant reference.
metric_relevance.nim: Net interest margin compressed from 2.7% in FY2023 to 2.4% in FY2026 Q2, with 2.5% in Q1. A thinner margin puts more weight on fee income and credit quality for earnings.
metric_relevance.noninterest_income: Noninterest income rose to $31.84B in FY2026 Q2 from $24.47B in Q1, mostly on the $4.6B Visa gain. The jump is not a clean run-rate step-up in fee income.
metric_relevance.npl_ratio: The nonperforming loan ratio was 0.7% at FY2025 Q4, flat with FY2024 Q4 and up from 0.5% at FY2023 Q4. Stable asset quality on this measure could be tested by the private credit loosening and card guidance changes.
metric_relevance.revenue: Total revenue peaked at $57.35B in FY2026 Q2 with the $4.6B Visa share exchange gain, then fell to $50.17B in FY2026 Q3. Underwriters should separate that one-time gain from the run-rate before reading the revenue trend.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_qoq: The 15.1% QoQ jump in FY2026 Q2 came in the same quarter as the $4.6B Visa share exchange gain, so the spike does not show underlying operating momentum.
metric_relevance.revenue_growth_yoy: YoY revenue growth of 27.7% in FY2026 Q2 follows -10.5% in FY2025 Q2, a swing that the Visa share exchange gain largely explains. Quarterly growth has been volatile, so the single-quarter figure is a weak signal.
metric_relevance.roa: ROA was 1.4% in FY2025, down from 1.5% in FY2024. The 2026 quarterly results include the one-time Visa gain, so the annual ratio will not show the run-rate profitability of the business.
metric_relevance.roe: ROE slipped to 16.1% in FY2025 from 17.4% in FY2024 while equity grew to $362.44B at year-end. Lower returns on a larger capital base sit alongside the buyback slowdown tied to keeping capital for deployment.
metric_relevance.tier1_ratio: The Tier 1 capital ratio fell from 16.8% at FY2024 Q4 to 15.1% at FY2026 Q2, moving in the same direction as the CET1 decline. This makes the capital trend a multi-ratio pattern rather than a single-ratio issue.
metric_relevance.uninsured_deposit_share: Uninsured deposits were 64.3% of total deposits in FY2026 Q2, up from 60.9% at FY2025 Q4 and 56.1% at FY2023 Q4. The rising share is the main funding-side risk underwriters should track, with estimated uninsured deposits of $1,743.90B.
metric_relevance.unrealized_loss_to_equity: Unrealized securities losses equal 4.9% of equity in FY2026 Q2, down from 7.8% at FY2024 Q4 and 12.6% at FY2022. The measure has narrowed sharply, though it is still a drag on the equity base.
